crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Ethics review with AI assistance covers the use of machine learning and natural language tools to support institutional review boards, research ethics committees, and journal editors in screening protocols, identifying risks, checking consent language, and flagging conflicts or missing safeguards. It sits within research integrity because the aim is to make review more consistent and thorough, not to replace human judgment. The scope includes pre-review triage, literature and precedent retrieval, and drafting structured comments, but final determinations remain with qualified reviewers.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These systems typically run on institutional servers or cloud platforms that can access the committee's document management system and a controlled corpus of past decisions, regulations, and guidance. Many deployments use retrieval-augmented generation over local policy libraries so that cited rules stay traceable, and they require role-based access because submissions contain sensitive personal data. Compute needs are modest compared with large model training, since most work is inference over text.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by breaking a submission into sections, extracting entities such as study population, data types, and consent provisions, then comparing those against a checklist of ethical requirements. Language models draft queries and summaries, while retrieval systems pull relevant precedent and regulation text for the reviewer to verify. Human reviewers edit or reject the machine's flags, and the system logs those corrections to improve future suggestions.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk turn on confidentiality, accountability, and the possibility of automation bias. Reviewers must treat AI output as advisory, and institutions need clear records of what the tool suggested and what the committee decided. Data protection rules apply to protocols and participant information, so access should be limited and audit trails kept. Provenance matters because any cited rule or precedent must link back to its source document rather than a search summary.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward more structured pre-review and continuous monitoring, where AI assistants help track approved studies for adverse events or protocol deviations and flag emerging ethical issues. Standards bodies are beginning to discuss how to validate these tools across different regulatory regimes, and the field is likely to move from generic language models to purpose-built systems trained on vetted ethics corpora. Human oversight will remain central, but the assistant's role may expand from drafting to real-time consistency checking across a portfolio of studies.
